transcript:
Meeting header
Date: 2025-10-22 15:00 PT
Duration: 47 minutes
Attendees: Samantha Chen (Redwood AE), Miguel Alvarez (Redwood SE), Priya Patel (Redwood Product), Alex Romero (Lighthouse), Tara Nguyen (Lighthouse), Jon Park (Lighthouse), Maya Singh (Lighthouse Sec)

Summary:
Quick hosted API walkthrough showing embeddings + reranker endpoints, Console demo of search metrics and Optimize suggestions, discussion of tradeoffs (latency vs cost, caching, dedicated capacity vs hosted), security questions around SSO/keys/audit logs, agreement to run a 1-week POC running Lighthouse's 5k query set against Redwood hosted embeddings + rerank pipeline.

Topics:
- Hosted embeddings endpoint (model selection, dimensionality)
- Rerank endpoint (batch scoring, streaming vs sync)
- Console: per-route latency & cost breakdown, Optimize suggestions for caching/quantization
- POC scope, timeline, and security/compliance checklist

Action items recap at end.

Transcript body:
00:00:00 Samantha: Hey everyone, thanks for joining, this is Sam from Redwood. quick round of intros?
00:00:07 Alex: Yeah Alex from Lighthouse. we run search for a bunch of media properties, need to improve relevance without blowing up cost.
00:00:14 Samantha: Awesome. Miguel and Priya are with me, Miguel will show the API and a rerank flow, Priya will show Console and Optimize.
00:00:25 Miguel: Great - I'll jump in on the demo. so first high-level: our hosted API exposes embeddings and a separate rerank endpoint. you can do a vector search externally then call rerank to rescore top candidates or call rerank-only with text pairs.
00:00:45 Tara: quick Q - do you host the vectors or do we host them?
00:00:50 Miguel: Both patterns supported. for hosted vectors we store encrypted vectors and manage indexing; for hybrid you can keep control and call our rerank endpoint with vectors you provide.
00:01:10 Jon: is there a length limit for documents or snippet sizes?
00:01:15 Miguel: not strict but embeddings model has token limits; larger docs we chunk. best practice is chunk + metadata.
00:01:35 Miguel: demoing the API: here's a sample embeddings call, model param is redwood-emb-small-v1, returns 1536 dims - we also offer 768d and 2048d options for cost/quality tradeoffs.
00:01:58 Alex: 1536 sounds heavy - we currently use 512. what's cost delta?
00:02:03 Priya: cost scales roughly with dims and token spend. Optimize will recommend smaller dims for high-volume queries where quality delta is small.
00:02:20 Miguel: moving to rerank - the endpoint accepts a list of candidate docs + query and returns scores and a reranked list. supporting batching of queries up to N and streaming results if you want incremental scores.
00:02:40 Maya: security: do you have KMS integration and key rotation?
00:02:44 Samantha: yes we integrate with customer KMS (AWS KMS/GCP KMS) and we support enterprise HSM in Private deployments. for hosted we offer envelope encryption and rotation policies.
00:03:05 Tara: audit logs?
00:03:07 Samantha: Console shows audit events, and we ship syslog/ELK sink for enterprise customers - full request-level audit available under dedicated contracts.
00:03:25 Miguel: moving to a quick live demo - hitting the embeddings endpoint with an example query about "how to submit an op ed".
00:03:40 Miguel: (typing) POST /v1/embeddings { model: redwood-emb-medium, input: "how to submit an op ed" } -> response shows vector and token count.
00:04:05 Alex: tokens look normal. how long to get vectors?
00:04:10 Miguel: median latency for that model is about 40-80ms in hosted multi-tenant for short queries, 20-40ms on dedicated pools depending on GPU.
00:04:25 Jon: what's a typical tail like? p95 or p99?
00:04:30 Miguel: p95 ~120ms, p99 depends on burst and cold-starts but we have warm pools. Console shows per-route p95/p99 metrics.
00:04:50 Priya: here's the Console - per-route cost and latency breakdown, tokens per request, and Optimize suggestions. you can see Optimize recommending prefix caching for repeated query prefixes and a quantization profile for the embedding model.
00:05:10 Alex: can you explain prefix caching?
00:05:15 Priya: prefix caching stores KV cache for popular prefixes for chat-style sessions - in search you'd use a smaller prefix cache for re-ranking to avoid recomputation in multi-turn flows. it helps for conversational search but less so for single-shot queries.
00:05:40 Tara: we heard "KV cash" in a previous demo, is that what you mean?
00:05:44 Miguel: yes sorry transcription - KV cache. sometimes speech-to-text flips it.
00:06:05 Alex: show us the rerank example?
00:06:10 Miguel: sure. I'm sending a rerank request with 10 candidates, we call /v1/rerank sync, it returns scores and picks the best order. Look at the payload size - we recommend trimming HTML and heavy markup and passing clean text.
00:06:33 Jon: do you re-embed inside rerank or work off similarity scores?
00:06:37 Miguel: rerank uses a cross-encoder style scoring for final quality - it re-encodes query+doc pairs. this is heavier but higher precision. you can also use a lightweight reranker that uses precomputed embeddings and a small model for speed.
00:06:58 Alex: tradeoff numbers?
00:07:02 Miguel: cross-encoder p50 latency on hosted is ~120-250ms depending on sequence length; lightweight rerank can be sub-30ms but sacrifices some quality.
00:07:20 Alex: so if we do top-100 retrieval and then rerank top-10 with cross encoder, latency will be?
00:07:25 Miguel: depends on parallelism and batch size. if you batch the 10 pairs you can push it down to ~150-300ms; if you stream per result it's higher.
00:07:45 Maya: any concerns about data residency? our legal team wants EU-only storage for vectors and logs.
00:07:52 Samantha: we support data residency - hosted in region-specific clusters and logs can be routed to your EU account. for strict EU-only, Dedicated or Private deployments are options.
00:08:20 Tara: throughput: our traffic is spiky around publishing windows; will hosted handle bursts?
00:08:27 Priya: hosted supports burst capacity; we have autoscaling and can route to overflow capacity. if you need guaranteed throughput, Dedicated reservations are recommended.
00:08:45 Alex: curious about cost — what's the unit economics on rerank versus retrieval?
00:08:50 Miguel: rough rule: retrieval (ANN) is cheap, embeddings compute is per-token + per-dim amortized; rerank cross-encoder is per-pair compute. we provide a per-call estimate in Console and Optimize will estimate per-route cost.
00:09:12 Jon: can we run a benchmark with our 5k queries?
00:09:16 Samantha: absolutely, we'd like that. Miguel can give you a runner script. we'll run against hosted and show results and cost.
00:09:30 Alex: security follow-ups: SSO, SAML, SCIM?
00:09:35 Maya: yes and does console have role-based access?
00:09:38 Samantha: we support SAML SSO, SCIM for user provisioning, RBAC with fine-grained roles, and per-token scoping. we'll include configuration docs in the follow-up.
00:09:55 Miguel: quick detour to Optimize - it scans your workload and suggests quantization, batching windows, and whether to move to a smaller embedding model with minimal quality loss.
00:10:10 Alex: show an Optimize suggestion?
00:10:14 Priya: here's a sample suggestion: switch redwood-emb-1536 -> redwood-emb-768 for high-volume daily queries, enable 8-bit quantization on rerank small model, enable prefix cache for repeated session flows. shows expected cost savings and estimated impact on relevance.
00:10:40 Tara: how do you measure impact on relevance?
00:10:45 Priya: we run A/B style evals against your labeled set and report delta in MRR/Recall@k; you can set tolerance thresholds for automatic rollouts.
00:11:05 Jon: will Optimize run automatically or is it run-on-demand?
00:11:09 Priya: both - you can run analyses on-demand or enable scheduled reviews; production rollouts still require approval.
00:11:25 Alex: about observability - can we get token-level cost by route? we need to show spend to product leads.
00:11:31 Samantha: yes per-route token & compute breakdown, traces and sample requests stored for a 30-day window by default. extended retention is an add-on.
00:11:50 Alex: if we start a POC, do we need to sign any NDA?
00:11:54 Samantha: standard data processing addendum available, and we can sign an NDA.
00:12:10 Miguel: demo - I'll run a small rerank workload live: sending 10 queries with top-50 retrieved candidates and rerank top-5.
00:12:30 Miguel: (shows request/response) Note the response includes per-item scores and a provenance field with snippet offsets.
00:12:50 Jon: provenance is great. can we get passage offsets in original doc?
00:12:55 Miguel: yes we return snippet offsets if you provide original doc ids and offsets.
00:13:10 Alex: are embeddings indexable for ANN search inside Redwood?
00:13:14 Miguel: yes we support built-in ANN with configurable index types; you can also export vectors to your own index provider.
00:13:35 Tara: earlier you said hybrid - can you expand?
00:13:38 Miguel: hybrid means you keep vectors in your system but call Redwood's rerank; or you use our vector store but control encryption keys and retention.
00:13:55 Maya: any SOC2 reports available?
00:13:58 Samantha: yes SOC2 Type II available for customers under NDA.
00:14:12 Alex: will the demo include Console walk-through of alerts?
00:14:16 Priya: yep, here's an example alert for relevance regression - it links to failing prompts and diffs in model outputs.
00:14:35 Miguel: small note on caching: prefix/KV cache helps multi-turn but for one-shot search you should use query caching for frequent queries; Optimize will detect hot queries.
00:14:55 Jon: about batching - what's recommended batch window for rerank?
00:15:00 Miguel: small window, 25-100ms for low-latency apps; larger windows increase throughput but add latency. Optimize recommends per-route windows.
00:15:20 Tara: do you expose model versions so we can pin in production?
00:15:23 Samantha: yes pin model versions and freeze rollouts; Console also supports canary and A/B rollouts.
00:15:40 Alex: what about on-prem or VPC? we have some regulated brands that might require private infra.
00:15:47 Samantha: we have Redwood Private for VPC/on-prem and can run an on-prem package for air-gapped environments. that includes a customer-managed control plane option.
00:16:10 Alex: ok let's talk costing model - is it per-token plus per-embedding-dim?
00:16:14 Miguel: yes per-token for generation-like actions, per-embedding request for embeddings with a small per-dim factor, and per-rerank-call compute. Console will estimate unit costs by route.
00:16:35 Jon: do you have burst credits or committed discounts for Seasonal spikes?
00:16:39 Priya: we offer burst credit buckets and committed Reserved capacity for predictable workloads. you can combine both.
00:16:55 Maya: audit & access question: can we get request logs for legal e-discovery?
00:17:00 Samantha: yes under enterprise plans we can provide longer retention and exportable logs for compliance.
00:17:19 Miguel: quick note - avoid sending PII into rerank if possible; we support field-level redaction and tokenization helpers.
00:17:35 Alex: we want to run a 1-week POC that will run your hosted pipeline against our 5k query set and compare MRR and cost.
00:17:43 Samantha: perfect. Tentative plan: Lighthouse provides dataset, Redwood runs baseline on hosted with redwood-emb-medium + rerank-cross, returns metrics and cost, then run Optimize suggestions (emb-768 + quantized small rerank) to show cost/quality tradeoff.
00:18:10 Tara: how do you handle rate limits during POC?
00:18:14 Samantha: we'll set up a scoped API key with increased quotas for the POC.
00:18:28 Miguel: I'll share a runner: simple Python script that posts batches and captures scores and timing.
00:18:38 Alex: can we simulate our traffic spikes?
00:18:41 Miguel: yes script supports burst patterns. also we can replay traffic from logs if you provide them.
00:19:00 Jon: are there any pitfalls from previous customers running similar POCs?
00:19:05 Miguel: two common pitfalls: sending heavy HTML into embeddings without cleaning, and not setting proper batch windows which increases latency.
00:19:20 Alex: what about cold-cache effects?
00:19:23 Priya: Optimize suggests warm-up runs; also prefix caching and warm pools reduce cold start impact.
00:19:40 Maya: encryption-at-rest verification?
00:19:43 Samantha: vectors are encrypted at rest; we can provide KMS attestation and encryption keys rotation docs.
00:20:04 Miguel: small demo of Console: here is a per-route dashboard showing token consumption, p95 latency, and an anomaly flagged by the quality monitor.
00:20:25 Priya: quality monitor uses your labeled evals and pass/fail thresholds and surfaces regressions. it links to failing prompts for triage.
00:20:45 Tara: is the quality monitor auto-triggered on model changes?
00:20:48 Priya: you can set auto-checks on rollouts and block if MRR drop > threshold.
00:21:05 Alex: on the rerank scoring - do you return logits or normalized probabilities?
00:21:09 Miguel: by default scores are normalized 0-1; we also optionally return raw logits in debug mode.
00:21:25 Jon: will that leak model internals?
00:21:28 Miguel: debug mode is tenant-restricted and should not be enabled in public-facing keys.
00:21:45 Maya: compliance: we need an SCP and data processing addendum.
00:21:50 Samantha: we'll send the DPA and SOC2 under NDA.
00:22:05 Miguel: a note on embeddings dimensionality - sometimes lower dims preserve enough signal for our customers, so Optimize will run automated downselection tests.
00:22:25 Alex: if we adopt smaller dims, do we lose recall on long-tail queries?
00:22:29 Priya: potentially; Optimize reports recall@k and you can set thresholds to avoid regressions on long-tail.
00:22:50 Jon: let's talk about instrumentation - how do we tag requests so we can tie to Lighthouse product metrics?
00:22:55 Miguel: you can pass metadata headers and trace ids; we also provide tracing hooks to correlate request traces with product logs.
00:23:20 Tara: what's the SLA on hosted endpoints?
00:23:24 Samantha: hosted has a best-effort SLA; Dedicated has contractual SLAs with uptime and latency targets.
00:23:40 Alex: for the POC we prefer hosted to test speed to value.
00:23:44 Samantha: that works. we'll scope a 1-week hosted pilot.
00:23:58 Miguel: quick technical detail - rerank cross-encoder uses attention that can be tuned for longer contexts, but costs scale roughly quadratically with seq length.
00:24:17 Jon: point taken. we'll try to limit context sizes.
00:24:30 Miguel: another note: you can precompute embeddings for documents and only compute live query embeddings which saves cost.
00:24:45 Alex: do you support incremental indexing for new content?
00:24:49 Miguel: yes incremental index updates supported with per-doc upserts.
00:25:05 Tara: licensing: do you restrict model use or fine-tuning?
00:25:08 Samantha: for hosted we offer curated open models and Redwood-verified variants; fine-tuning is available as an add-on for private deployments.
00:25:25 Alex: any chance you support Pinecone-like managed index connectors?
00:25:29 Miguel: we provide connectors to common vector stores including Pinecone, Milvus, and our own managed index.
00:25:50 Jon: let's capture next steps - we'll share dataset, Redwood will run runner, share results and pricing.
00:25:58 Samantha: noted. Miguel will send the script, I'll send security docs and pricing.
00:26:10 Alex: great. quick final question - does Redwood surface per-query reason codes for rerank decisions?
00:26:15 Miguel: we return a simple provenance snippet and score. we also provide an explain API in debug mode that highlights tokens contributing to score but that's tenant-only and higher-cost.
00:26:35 Tara: that explain API sounds useful. we'll flag it for the POC.
00:26:50 Maya: any red flags on privacy if we send user-generated content?
00:26:54 Samantha: we'll recommend redaction of PII in transit; for sensitive content consider Private deployment.
00:27:10 Miguel: time check - we still have about 20 minutes; want to deep dive into batching and a quick live benchmark run?
00:27:18 Alex: yes please.
00:27:25 Miguel: ok I'll kick off a small runner now against a 50-query sample to show timings and then we'll talk configuration knobs.
00:27:40 Miguel: (runs script) sending 50 queries with top-20 retrieval, reranking top-5 cross-encoder with batch size 10.
00:28:05 Miguel: results coming in - avg end-to-end latency ~210ms, p95 ~370ms for this config.
00:28:20 Jon: can you change batch window to 50ms?
00:28:24 Miguel: bumping window... rerun...
00:28:50 Miguel: new run avg latency ~180ms, throughput up slightly but p95 still depends on contention.
00:29:10 Alex: cool. can you show Optimize's recommended batch window?
00:29:14 Priya: Optimize suggests 30-80ms for this workload - it picked 50ms as a sweet spot.
00:29:35 Tara: what about model quantization on rerank small model?
00:29:38 Priya: 8-bit quantization reduced compute by ~2.5x in our tests with small quality delta. Optimize shows expected MRR delta.
00:29:58 Alex: will quantized models be slower for some queries?
00:30:02 Miguel: sometimes numerics change but generally quantization improves throughput and reduces memory footprint.
00:30:20 Jon: can we plug our evaluation harness into your Console to run nightly checks?
00:30:24 Priya: yes you can push eval datasets and schedule runs; results show up in Console with diffs.
00:30:40 Tara: let's confirm POC timeline once more?
00:30:44 Samantha: Lighthouse to send dataset by Oct 28, Redwood to run baseline and optimized runs Nov 3-7, results shared Nov 10, follow-up meeting Nov 12.
00:31:05 Alex: agreed.
00:31:12 Miguel: quick note on telemetry - we can add a request header to mark POC traffic so it's isolated for cost reporting.
00:31:25 Samantha: good catch.
00:31:40 Jon: any blockers from our side? we need legal to sign the DPA.
00:31:45 Maya: we'll push the DPA through, aim to sign by Oct 27.
00:32:00 Samantha: perfect. I'll send the security pack and SOC2 link after NDA.
00:32:10 Miguel: one more deep-dive point - reranker batch scoring supports GPU parallelization and we choose kernels based on sequence shape; we also do attention kernel selection to optimize speed.
00:32:34 Alex: that sounds like what you do at the infra side. any tenant limits on concurrent rerank calls?
00:32:39 Miguel: there are soft concurrency limits which we can raise for POCs.
00:32:55 Tara: ok we have a few questions on data retention that we'll email.
00:32:59 Samantha: send them to me and Maya will include them in the security packet.
00:33:15 Alex: final ask - can you include a simple cost forecast for our monthly expected volume?
00:33:20 Priya: yes we'll include cost forecast and a sensitivity table showing different embed dims and rerank choices.
00:33:40 Miguel: any other technical questions?
00:33:45 Jon: how do you handle model drift detection?
00:33:48 Priya: quality monitor watches labeled evals and production sampling; it flags drift and can roll back.
00:34:05 Alex: perfect. if no further questions, let's do a short wrap.
00:34:10 Samantha: wrap - recap next steps: Redwood send security docs, runner script, and pricing; Lighthouse share dataset and sign DPA; schedule POC kickoff week of Nov 3.
00:34:30 Alex: thanks everyone.
00:34:35 Miguel: thanks, I'll follow up with the script and sample payloads.
00:34:42 Priya: I'll include Optimize export for the suggested configs.
00:34:50 Maya: thanks all.
00:35:00 (meeting tails with informal chatter)

End of transcript.
